00012| Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
00013| 
00014| ## Usage
00015| 
00016| To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
00017| 
00018| ```ts filename="next.config.ts"
00019| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00020| 
00021| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00022|   cacheComponents: true,
00023| }
00024| 
00025| export default nextConfig
00026| ```
00027| 
00028| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
00029| 
00030| - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
00031| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
00032| - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
00033| 
00034| > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
00035| 
00036| Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
00037| 
00038| Read [How rendering works](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#how-rendering-works) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
00039| 
00040| > **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
00041| 
00042| ## Navigation with Activity
00043| 
00044| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
00045| 
00046| Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
00047| 
00048| - Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
00049| - When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
00050| - Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
00051| 
00052| This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
00055| 
00056| Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
00057| 
00058| ## Version History
00059| 
00060| | Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
00061| | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00062| | 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
